title: Birth in New Orleans and first interest in piano
summary: Robichaux gives his birth date and place and recalls hearing the piano player Game Kid at his mother's piano and at parties, and studying music at New Orleans University.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, this is Joe Robichaud from New Orleans, Louisiana.
I was born right here in New Orleans, around St. Mary and Camp, right in Magazine Market.
What was the date you were born?
You can just sit back and relax. I'll pick up everything. Can you remember the first music, how you got interested in music? The first music you heard?

Well, I'll tell you how I actually got interested in playing music. I was quite a young kid and I had a piano player that used to call Game Kid. And my mother had a piano in that time, I think it was around about 1907. And I was quite small and he used to come and play the piano. And at that time, all the piano players were very famous around New Orleans at that time. And I kind of liked the piano, but I didn't, I wasn't interested in learning then, but I used to just like to listen. And I met a little fellow that called Cooney. He used to play piano. And every Sunday he used to come up around Santa Anax, Hilda Santa Anax's house. And they used to have parties that I used to go to. And then I got interested in him and I used to go around with him. But I never tried to play at that time. But I loved it, but I didn't play it. I think about learning to play then rather. So in school, they was teaching music. I was attending New Orleans University then. And everybody had to learn a little bit about music.
Was that up on St. Charles Avenue?
That was on St. Charles Avenue.
I took a picture of that once.
